transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Sarah Nguyen (Orchid Head of ML), Raj Patel (Orchid CTO), Alex Chen (Orchid DevOps), Priya Rao (Orchid Procurement)

Summary:
Redwood and Orchid Health discussed renewal options and an expansion request: 2x dedicated capacity, adding EU region for regulatory/data residency, and a 12-month contract extension. Action items defined for pricing, benchmarks, and procurement timeline. Some discussion around VPC/private deployment considerations and fallback routing to hosted for burst.

Topics:
- Capacity upgrade / Dedicated capacity sizing
- Additional region (EU) and data residency
- Contract extension (term & pricing)
- Benchmarks: latency / cost tradeoffs, KV cache behavior
- Security / compliance notes (audit logs, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Quick roll call — Maya and Ethan here from Redwood.
[00:05] Sarah Nguyen: Hi, Sarah here.
[00:07] Raj Patel: Raj on the call.
[00:09] Alex Chen: Alex, yep.
[00:10] Priya Rao: Priya here.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Great. The goal today is to run through renewal options and the expansion asks we saw in your note; specifically two things, growth in capacity and adding the EU region. Wanted to hear context and timeline from you.
[00:25] Sarah Nguyen: Yeah, we've been seeing heavier traffic month over month, particularly our clinical summarization pipeline — tokens per request have gone up and we hit queuing on the dedicated pool during peak hours. We need at least 2x baseline capacity and ideally EU for GDPR/data locality for a subset of our customers.
[00:40] Ethan Cole: Got it. Do you have current throughput numbers? qps or tokens per second?
[00:44] Alex Chen: We're averaging about 80 rps at peak, bursts to 160 for 5–10 minutes, median sequence 550 tokens, with a long tail to 2,000. We posted some of that in the traffic csv earlier. Sorry the transcriber munged that, I sent it to Maya.
[00:58] Maya Patel: Yep we have the file. That pattern explains why continous batching is hitting limits; the dedicated pool needs more headroom or smarter pre-warming. For EU region, we can stand up an EU dedicated pool and route EU customers there. There's a bunch of options — dedicated in EU, or keep data in EU while routing inference to us in US with KMS key residency — but legal prefers compute in-region.
[01:20] Raj Patel: Compute in-region is the ask. Also curious about fallback behavior — if EU capacity is full, do we fail or route to US? We need fail-safe that doesn't leak data.
[01:30] Ethan Cole: Good question. We have smart routing rules: you can set policy to prefer EU and fallback to a compatible model variant that runs in US but with no customer data persisted; however, for strict residency you can set 'no-fallback'. We'll document that. There might be higher latency if we route to US.
[01:45] Sarah Nguyen: For some regulated payers, no-fallback is required. For others we can tolerate fallback with redaction.
[01:51] Priya Rao: Timeline wise procurement needs a signed amendment by end of next week to align with budget.
[01:56] Maya Patel: Understood. We can push a draft amendment for the 12-month extension with 2x capacity and EU add-on; I'll include pricing scenarios: flat committed vs tiered bursting.
[02:05] Sarah Nguyen: Pricing — high level, what changes if we go from hosted to Dedicated double capacity? Also curious about cost per token with quantization changes.
[02:12] Ethan Cole: Typically dedicated incurs a committed reservation, so unit costs are lower than hosted for steady workloads. With 2x capacity you'll pay for reserved nodes; we can mix reserved and burst pool. Quantization (like int8) helps but depends on model; we'll recommend profiles after benchmarking.
[02:28] Alex Chen: Are there known perf deltas between EU region GPUs and US? We prefer a single SKU for predictability.
[02:33] Ethan Cole: Performance varies by hardware availability — we'll match similar instance types where possible. We'll run a benchmark against EU nodes to quantify. For KV cache behavior, local cache warms will differ across regions, but we can enable cross-region warmers if you want.
[02:47] Raj Patel: What's the SLA uplift for Dedicated?
[02:50] Maya Patel: Dedicated comes with our SLA — 99.9% monthly uptime and latency SLOs per route; we can scope a higher SLA as an add-on. We'll capture that in the amendment.
[02:59] Sarah Nguyen: Security questions: KMS integration, audit logs retention, and SOC2 scope — we've got a compliance review next week. Can you send the SOC2 and ISO docs?
[03:08] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll attach the SOC 2 type II report, ISO summary, and details on KMS/HSM support. Note: sometimes transcriber writes K-M-S as KMS and the team gets confused, ha.
[03:18] Priya Rao: Also need to know encryption at rest for logs and retention windows.
[03:21] Ethan Cole: Logs are stored per your retention policy; for Private deployments the customer controls retention. For Dedicated hosted we can configure retention and deliver audit exports.
[03:30] Sarah Nguyen: For this contract we want 12 months, auto-renew unless either party gives 60 days notice. Any issues with that?
[03:36] Maya Patel: That's standard; we'll draft with those terms and highlight termination and exit obligations, including KV cache handover and model artifacts.
[03:43] Alex Chen: On the benchmark — can you simulate our token distribution? The long tail to 2k tokens skews GPU memory and KV cache usage.
[03:50] Ethan Cole: Yes, Ethan will run a benchmark using your test set with the same sequence distributions; we'll test EU and US regions and share latency and cost per 1M tokens.
[03:59] Raj Patel: Any concerns about model variants? We use a quantized variant in prod — will Redwood support our exact artifact?
[04:05] Ethan Cole: We support pinned model versions and customer artifacts; if you want a quantized build we can onboard it — there may be a short validation pass. We'll capture that in the onboarding checklist.
[04:14] Sarah Nguyen: One risk I want to flag: if Dedicated is 2x, but traffic grows 3x in six months, what's the path to scale quickly?
[04:20] Maya Patel: We have burst capacity and autoscaling; you can configure autoscale thresholds or a hybrid model: reserved baseline and burst to hosted or shared dedicated pool. For strict data residency we can only burst within the region unless you accept fallback.
[04:33] Priya Rao: Procurement question — will pricing for EU region be different because of infra costs?
[04:37] Maya Patel: Typically EU infra has a slight premium; we'll show both combined and itemized pricing in the amendment.
[04:44] Sarah Nguyen: Great. Can we also get a short doc that explains routing policies and the fallout modes? DevOps needs it.
[04:50] Ethan Cole: I'll produce a short one-pager with diagrams: prefer-in-region, no-fallback, and fallback-to-variant.
[04:57] Maya Patel: To recap next steps: I'll draft amendment and pricing, Ethan will run benchmarks and produce the routing one-pager, Alex will share token distribution, and Priya will confirm procurement timeline. We aim to have signed amendment by 2026-11-24.
[05:12] Raj Patel: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[05:15] Maya Patel: No blockers; we just need the traffic csv and confirmation of model artifacts.
[05:20] Sarah Nguyen: We'll send the CSV and model info by EOD tomorrow.
[05:23] Maya Patel: Excellent. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and a proposed time for the benchmark kickoff.
[05:29] Priya Rao: Thanks.
[05:31] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional name mis-hearings, e.g., Redwood -> Red wood or Ruedwood in transcript; some acronyms spelled out by speakers then transcribed inconsistently (KMS, VPC, KV cache).
